topic: AI capex shows as GDP drag (Fortune)
angle: Don’t confuse near-term accounting optics with long-term AI value—plan the runway.
sourceTitle: U.S. economy grows at sluggish 1.5% pace in second quarter
linkedinPost:
AI can make your quarter look worse before it makes your business better.

Fortune notes GDP grew 1.5%, and the surge in computer chip and AI investment shipments actually sliced 1.64 percentage points off the number. Accounting optics, not lack of activity.

Executives feel the same tension: imported GPUs hit cash and margins now, benefits arrive later and unevenly. That’s not a reason to pause—it’s a reason to manage the runway and measure the right leading indicators.

My playbook with clients:
- Stage-gate capex by use case, not by hardware tranche
- Track decision/cycle time, containment rate, and assisted-NPS as early signals
- Tie variable cloud/GPU spend to unit economics (per ticket, per claim, per lead)
- Pre-commit decommission plans for unused capacity

If your board only sees spend, you’ll starve the programs right before value shows up. If they see a clear path from infrastructure → workflow changes → measurable outcomes, you’ll keep patience and funding.

What’s on your AI scorecard that proves value is compounding—even before the P&L catches up? #AITransformation #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI
xPost: AI spend can dent near-term optics (ask GDP), then pay back in workflows. Fund by use case, track decision time/containment/NPS, tie GPU costs to unit economics. Manage the runway, not the headline. #AIStrategy
